![](/assets/images/discrete-math.png){fig-alt="Illustration of graphs, trees, and overlapping sets in blue and gold" width=1672 height=941 style="width:100%; height:auto;"}

Hi, I am RJ Nieto, and I will be your instructor for this module. I graduated
with a BSc in Mathematics with first-class honours from the University of
Bristol in the United Kingdom. I am currently pursuing an MSc in Applied and
Computational Mathematics at The Johns Hopkins University in the United States.

You can simply call me RJ, Kuya RJ, or Sir—though “Sir” sounds a little icky
because I have not been knighted by King Charles.
Please spare me Tito RJ or Daddy RJ, though.

I will use this page to share course information, lecture notes, examples,
exercises, and supplementary material for our *Discrete Structures* module at
Bulacan State University's Bustos Campus. As first-year BS Information
Technology students, you will use these materials throughout the semester.

To be frank, this course is discrete mathematics. Whatever the title may
suggest to you, you should expect a demanding first-year mathematics course.
I expect everyone to engage deeply with the material. The keys to mastering
mathematics are:

1. **Practice, constant practice.** Work through problems yourself and revisit
   the ones you find difficult.
2. **Curiosity.** Ask questions, even when they sound silly to you.
3. **Diligence.** Keep up with the material and work through your mistakes.

We will not be solving Olympiad-level problems, and you do not need exceptional
mathematical aptitude to do well here. Think of this module as functional
mathematical literacy for future IT specialists. We will work with logic,
sets, functions, relations, counting, integers, induction, recursion, graphs,
and trees, connecting these ideas to organising records, expressing access
rules, and modelling networks.

If you want to learn how to wrangle information, mathematics will give you the
tools to do it precisely and systematically.

BulSU aims to be a globally competitive university, and I want you to take
pride in your studies. Drawing on my own experience, particularly in the
United Kingdom, I will teach you with the same expectations of independent
study, careful reasoning, and active participation that I encountered at a
leading university abroad.

## Primary textbook

Oscar Levin's *Discrete Mathematics: An Open Introduction*, fourth edition,
is our primary textbook. It is available to read online or download as a free
PDF. We will use selected sections in the order shown below, with short
supplementary examples where needed.

[Open Levin's textbook — fourth edition](https://discrete.openmathbooks.org/dmoi4.html){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg target="_blank" rel="noopener"}

## Schedule

The semester begins on 16 November 2026; our first Saturday class is on
21 November. The tentative schedule below allows for 14 teaching sessions,
excluding the examination periods, Christmas break, and the
[national holidays on 6 February and 27 March 2027](https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/7/102791).
Coverage may be adjusted to allow more practice where needed. Exact examination
arrangements will be communicated through official class channels.

| Date | Topic | Levin reference |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| 21 November 2026 | Orientation; statements, connectives, truth tables, and implication | §§1.1–1.2 |
| 28 November 2026 | Equivalence, quantifiers, valid arguments, counterexamples, and introductory proof methods | Selected §§1.1–1.4 |
| 5 December 2026 | Sets, subsets, operations, Venn diagrams, and Cartesian products | §0.2; selected §5.1 |
| 12 December 2026 | Functions, domain and codomain, injectivity, surjectivity, composition, and inverses | §0.2; selected §5.2 |

| 6 March 2027 | Graphs, paths, cycles, connectivity, and representations; application task introduced | Selected §2.1; supplementary examples |
| 13 March 2027 | Trees, rooted trees, spanning trees, and introductory breadth-first traversal | Selected §2.2 |
| 20 March 2027 | Application workshop, consolidation, and final revision | Selected exercises |
| 27 March 2027 | **Black Saturday: no class** | — |
| 29 March–3 April 2027 | **Final examination period** | — |

## Course policies

These class arrangements should be read alongside the
[BulSU Undergraduate Student Manual](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ew8hDsW_anZjLsZJKI3rEKAnhT1K4OTd/view)
(Part II, Sections F–G and J–L) and the
[Enhanced Guidelines on Student Conduct, Discipline, and Grievance Intervention](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1FA3IPniUsXfeqscEyS_FdN356I_EwxGm/view),
which BulSU identifies as approved under BOR Resolution No. 34, series of 2022.
The approved syllabus and applicable university policies take precedence over
these class arrangements.

1. **Electronic devices:** Phones and other personal electronic devices must
   be switched off and put away during class. Approved accessibility
   arrangements and university-required exceptions take precedence.
2. **Photo:** Please bring a **recent 1×1 photo** to our first class. This will
   help me identify students when recording attendance.
3. **Seating:** We will use a **fixed seating plan** to facilitate
   attendance-taking and the recording of class recitation.
4. **Attention and classroom conduct:** We meet only once a week for three
   hours, so each session can be more cognitively demanding than a shorter
   class that meets twice a week. I expect everyone to listen intently and
   stay focused, even when the material gets difficult. If you are struggling
   to follow, you are strongly encouraged to interrupt me and ask questions,
   or raise them during consultation hours. Disruptive chatting, excessive
   noise, and other misbehaviour are unacceptable and will be addressed through
   the university's prescribed disciplinary procedures. Participation marks
   follow the approved assessment criteria. I am training you for real life,
   and success in real life requires discipline.
5. **Coursework and deadlines:** Submit coursework by the stated deadline.
   Work not submitted by the deadline receives **zero marks**, unless an
   excused absence or another university-approved arrangement applies. An
   unexcused absence does not extend a deadline or entitle you to a make-up
   assessment. Work submitted on time is assessed under the published criteria.
6. **Attendance and punctuality:** Attend promptly and regularly. The handbook
   marks arrival 15 minutes after the scheduled start as tardy and 20 minutes
   after the start as absent; being marked absent does not prevent you from
   attending the lesson. Unexcused absences exceeding **20% of required class
   time before midterms** trigger automatic dropping, recorded as **FDA
   (failure due to absences) or UD (unofficially dropped)**. Against the current
   42-hour teaching timetable, a third full-session absence totals nine hours
   and exceeds 20%; keep unexcused absences to **no more than two sessions**.
   The official calculation follows the required semester contact hours, and
   the count does not reset after midterms. Attendance classifications and
   grades follow university rules; FDA/UD and a numerical grade of 5.0 are
   distinct classifications.
7. **Missed examinations:** If you miss an examination for an excused reason,
   contact me promptly with supporting documentation. Special examinations
   require the instructor's recommendation and the unit head's approval under
   Part II, Section J. Your final examination is **not automatically
   double-weighted**. An unexcused missed examination receives **zero marks**
   under the course assessment arrangements, subject to applicable university
   policies.
8. **Excused absences:** The handbook recognises official university
   representation, medically certified sickness, and force majeure as excused
   reasons. Notify me promptly and provide the relevant documentation. An
   excused absence does not waive coursework requirements; arrange to complete
   missed work. The handbook also sets a **30% limit on excused absences**.
9. **Assessment and concerns:** Assessment components, weights, and marking
   criteria follow the approved syllabus. You may ask how your marks were
   calculated and request a review of your class standing. Raise concerns with
   me or use the university's student grievance procedure.
10. **Borderline marks:** I may extend consideration to students with
    borderline failing marks who have **perfect attendance**, where permitted
    by the approved assessment rules. This is discretionary and does not
    guarantee a passing grade or waive academic requirements.

Course-specific arrangements and updates will be communicated through official
class channels.
